sumInsured: Not specified (as per Policy Schedule / Schedule of Coverage)

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: We will pay for the Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred during the 60 days immediately before Hospitalization
great.reference: Section B, I Hospitalization Cover, 4. Pre-hospitalization cover (around page 10)
great.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for 60 days immediately before hospitalization. This helps pay for consultations, tests and medicines leading up to admission.

great.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: We will pay for the Post-HospitalizationMedical Expenses incurred upto180 days from the date Insured Person is discharged from Hospital
great.reference: Section B, I Hospitalization Cover, 5. Post-Hospitalization cover (around page 10)
great.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 180 days from the date of discharge. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for follow-ups and medicines during recovery.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: On each Renewal of the Policy with Us, We will apply 5% of Basic Sum Insured... Cumulative Bonus will be reduced at the same rate as accrued in the event of admissible Claim... Cumulative Bonus can be accumulated upto 50% of Basic Sum Insured.
great.reference: Section B, II Renewal Benefits, 2. Cumulative Bonus (around page 11)
great.explanation: A 5% cumulative bonus is added on each claim-free renewal, up to 50% of the Basic Sum Insured, and it reduces by the same rate when a claim is paid. This means your bonus does not reset to zero after a claim, which preserves some extra cover.

good.name: Built-in SI Buffer
good.quote: We will pay for Medical Expenses incurred and admissible under Section B-I-1,up to additional Sum Insured equivalent to Basic Sum Insured... Claim under this Cover is admissible only when total of Basic Sum Insuredis completely utilized.
good.reference: Section B, III Optional Covers, 9. Major Illness Hospitalization Expenses (around page 16)
good.explanation: An additional Sum Insured equal to the Basic Sum Insured is available, but only after the Basic Sum Insured is completely used. This provides extra protection for large claims, but it is not usable for the first claim until the base limit is exhausted.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 48 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.reference: Section C, 1.I Waiting Periods, i) Pre-existing Diseases – Code – Excl01 (around page 19)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after 48 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This is a standard 4-year waiting period, so plan coverage accordingly if you have known conditions.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.
good.reference: Section C, 1.I Waiting Periods, ii) Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period – Code – Excl02 (around page 19)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is in line with common market practice for such conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.reference: Section C, 1.I Waiting Periods, iii) 30-day waiting period – Code – Excl03 (around page 20)
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy commencement, except accidents. This is a standard initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: Not found in provided policy wording excerpt.
bad.reference: Document review: Section B Benefits & Optional Covers (no restore/reinstatement/restoration clause found).
bad.explanation: No restoration/reinstatement of Sum Insured is mentioned in the provided wording excerpt. This means once the Sum Insured is used up in a policy year, further hospitalization claims may not be payable unless another benefit adds extra cover.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as Food charges... laundry charges, attendant charges... Full list of Non-Medical expenses is attached... Annexure I - List of Non-Medical Expenses ... (includes) GLOVES ... NEBULISATION KIT ... ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED...
bad.reference: Section C, 2.II Specific Permanent Exclusions, xii) Non-Medical expenses (around page 21) and Annexure I lists (around pages 32-34)
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items (e.g., gloves, nebulisation kit and other kits) are excluded as per the annexure list. This can increase your out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization even when the main treatment is covered.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Insured Person shall bear specified percentage of admissible Claim amount under each and every Claim If Co-payment is applicable
bad.reference: Section B, I Hospitalization Cover (appears repeatedly, around pages 10-11)
bad.explanation: A co-payment can apply, where you bear a specified percentage of every admissible claim amount if it is applicable. This is a negative because it can reduce every claim payout and increase your share of costs.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: Room rent, boarding and Nursing charges

unclear.explanation: Room rent is listed as covered, but the entitlement/limit is not stated in the provided quote. Your actual room category or any cap would need to be confirmed from the Policy Schedule.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless facility can be availed only at Our Network Provider. The complete list of Network Providers... is available on Our website
unclear.reference: Section E, Claim Procedure, 'Conditions for obtaining Cashless facility' (around page 30)
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at the insurer’s network providers, with the list hosted on the website. Since the number of hospitals is not stated, the breadth of the cashless network cannot be graded from the wording alone.
